report: Source reassessment: all three ordinary implementation entries in parser.rs and both ordinary annotated tests cover the complete comma claim. value_fields serves struct fields and named enum payloads; the enum declaration loop serves variants; type_list serves tuple payload elements. Each loop accepts its closing delimiter immediately after a member, otherwise requires a comma, then accepts the closing delimiter at the next iteration. This enforces adjacent-member separators and permits either trailing-comma form. The examples illustrate those same rules, including single fields and prose; illustrative unresolved names do not require a closed model. member_lists_require_separators_and_allow_trailing_commas visibly tests both trailing forms for structs, variants, tuple payloads and named payloads, and rejects omitted separators in all four categories. Captured parse_body/check helpers show successful cases must parse (unwrap) before validation and invalid cases check parser errors directly. rejects_malformed_value_declarations additionally asserts errors for missing struct-field and tuple-payload separators; its other malformed declarations are supplementary. These assertions would detect acceptance of missing commas or rejection of optional trailing forms. No TODO/N/A entries or deferred prerequisites exist. Baseline: independently verified exact current bytes against historical implementation_sources/parser.rs and both test_sources files; the historical rationale remains sufficient after current claim, metadata, test-body and helper inspection. Execution: ran review start, recorded reads and a byte-comparison script; no behavioral tests or build were run by this reviewer. Coordinator-reported 321 passing sage-meta tests and root build are separate execution evidence. No source edits or requested changes.
